blocks.text: An operator is part of a type’s public language. If a + b behaves like arithmetic, readers can use familiar reasoning. If it unexpectedly opens a file, mutates both operands, or performs an unrelated conversion, the short spelling hides more than it clarifies. HarborWorks uses a bounded quantity type to show how natural syntax can preserve domain rules rather than bypass them.

blocks.text: The chapter’s quantity is deliberately small: its permitted values lie between minus one million and one million. Its arithmetic rejects results outside that domain. This is not a currency library, a physical-units system, or a universal overflow wrapper. The narrow domain makes the meaning of equality, ordering, arithmetic, and stream extraction independently testable.

topics.title: 7.1 Overloading Arithmetic and Comparison Operators
topics.summary: An overloaded operator is a function selected through operator syntax. It cannot invent a new operator symbol or change the language’s precedence rules. Its meaning should remain close enough to the conventional operation that a reader can reason about an expression without opening every definition.

blocks.text: This separates representation overflow from domain overflow. For arbitrary integer operands, the addition would need checks before evaluation to avoid signed overflow. A constructor cannot repair undefined behavior that already occurred while computing its argument. Later generic arithmetic examples make the precheck explicit for full integer ranges.

blocks.text: Begin with the result contract. Adding two quantities should not alter either operand. The result should represent their mathematical sum when that sum is within the type’s accepted range, and it should reject the operation otherwise. These requirements suggest a nonmutating binary operator returning a new value. A compound assignment such as += would have a different mutation contract and should preserve its target on failure if that is what the type promises.

blocks.text: Check representability before relying on arithmetic in the implementation type. A constructor that rejects an out-of-range result cannot repair signed overflow that already occurred while computing that result. The example restricts both operands and explicitly requires an integer representation large enough for their intermediate sum. A general checked arithmetic type needs bounds checks or a suitable wider representation before the addition, not only validation afterward.

blocks.text: An explicit constructor prevents accidental conversions from unrelated integers at arbitrary call sites. Requiring Quantity{3} can make a unit or domain choice visible. This does not mean all implicit conversions are wrong; it means conversions belong to the type’s interface and should be justified by the domain rather than included to save a few characters in a demonstration.

Document the bounded domain instead of claiming the type implements unrestricted integer mathematics.

topics.title: 7.1.2 Defining Meaningful Comparisons
topics.summary: The defaulted three-way comparison compares the quantity’s value representation and supplies a coherent ordering for this type. Equality is consistent with that value model: two quantities with the same accepted integer are equal.

cards.question: Explain Defining Meaningful Comparisons in your own words.
cards.answer: The defaulted three-way comparison compares the quantity’s value representation and supplies a coherent ordering for this type. Equality is consistent with that value model: two quantities with the same accepted integer are equal.

blocks.text: 7.1.2 Defining Meaningful Comparisons
rich: 7.1.2 Defining Meaningful Comparisons

blocks.text: The defaulted three-way comparison compares the quantity’s value representation and supplies a coherent ordering for this type. Equality is consistent with that value model: two quantities with the same accepted integer are equal.
rich: The defaulted three-way comparison compares the quantity’s value representation and supplies a coherent ordering for this type. Equality is consistent with that value model: two quantities with the same accepted integer are equal.

blocks.text: Do not default comparison blindly for a type containing caches, raw ownership addresses, or fields that are not part of its logical value. Memberwise ordering is only appropriate when member order expresses the intended semantics. Floating-point types can also have partial-order concerns such as NaN, unlike this bounded integer model. Define the ordering relation required by algorithms and containers before selecting an implementation.
rich: Do not default comparison blindly for a type containing caches, raw ownership addresses, or fields that are not part of its logical value. Memberwise ordering is only appropriate when member order expresses the intended semantics. Floating-point types can also have partial-order concerns such as NaN, unlike this bounded integer model. Define the ordering relation required by algorithms and containers before selecting an implementation.

blocks.text: Equality asks whether two values mean the same thing under the type’s contract. Ordering asks how values should be arranged. Those relations often use the same fields for a simple quantity, but a larger record can have several meaningful orderings. A task’s identity might be its ID, while a displayed report sorts by priority and then ID. Defining one global operator for every possible report ordering can make the model misleading.

A task’s identity might be its ID, while a displayed report sorts by priority and then ID. Defining one global operator for every possible report ordering can make the model misleading.

blocks.text: The defaulted three-way comparison in the quantity delegates to its integer member, giving a natural ordering for the represented value. For a record with several members, a defaulted comparison considers the members in declaration order according to the language rules. That order is a design decision when exposed publicly. Reordering fields for layout should not silently redefine business ordering unless that is intentionally part of the API change.

blocks.text: Floating-point members deserve additional attention because NaNs do not behave like ordinary totally ordered numbers. A sorting comparator must still satisfy the algorithm’s requirements over the inputs it actually accepts. Rejecting non-finite values at a domain boundary, using a defined total-order policy, or selecting an appropriate comparison relation can be necessary. Do not assume a spaceship token makes every numeric domain safely sortable.

blocks.text: For HarborWorks, keep report ordering as an explicit projection or comparator when it represents a presentation choice rather than the intrinsic meaning of a task. This reduces the chance that one report’s sorting policy will accidentally control a set, map, or another part of the application with different identity needs.

blocks.text: A formatter should document whether its output is intended for humans, round-trip serialization, or both. This example’s integer form can be read by its extractor, but it does not define a versioned file format. More complex domain types need delimiters, escaping, units, and compatibility rules that a convenient insertion overload does not supply automatically.

blocks.text: An insertion operator should return the stream it received so operations can be chained. Its output should be documented: raw numeric value, units, diagnostic decoration, or a stable interchange record are different formats. The quantity’s operator emits only its integer value. That makes it suitable for simple composition, but it is not a promise of a complete self-describing file format.
rich: An insertion operator should return the stream it received so operations can be chained. Its output should be documented: raw numeric value, units, diagnostic decoration, or a stable interchange record are different formats. The quantity’s operator emits only its integer value. That makes it suitable for simple composition, but it is not a promise of a complete self-describing file format.

blocks.text: The stream already has formatting state. Base selection, precision, fill characters, locale, and error state can affect output. A type that changes persistent formatting settings should decide whether to restore them. Otherwise printing one quantity can change how a later unrelated value is formatted. A diagnostic helper with a local string stream can isolate formatting choices when predictable text matters more than reusing every caller setting.

A diagnostic helper with a local string stream can isolate formatting choices when predictable text matters more than reusing every caller setting.

blocks.text: Insertion can fail because the destination fails. Returning the stream allows the caller to inspect its state or use an exception mask. Do not clear a failed output stream inside a value’s insertion operator merely to make the operator appear successful. The operator should cooperate with the stream’s error model, leaving publication and retry policy to an appropriate outer boundary.

blocks.text: The extractor follows formatted stream conventions, so it may accept a numeric prefix and leave trailing characters for later parsing. A complete-record parser must separately require the intended end of input, as Book I’s from_chars example did. Stream extraction and whole-field validation are different interfaces; do not claim that this operator rejects every trailing suffix by itself.

blocks.text: Extraction should parse into a candidate and commit only after the candidate is acceptable. In the quantity operator, failure to read an integer leaves the target unchanged. A representable integer outside the quantity domain sets failbit and also preserves the old value. The existing value remains available for the caller’s recovery logic.

reading.title: 7.2.2 Reading Objects with operator>>
paragraphs: operator>> reads into a local candidate. If extraction succeeds but the candidate violates the quantity range, it sets failbit and leaves the previous quantity unchanged. If extraction itself fails, the destination is likewise preserved.

The extractor follows formatted stream conventions, so it may accept a numeric prefix and leave trailing characters for later parsing. A complete-record parser must separately require the intended end of input, as Book I’s from_chars example did. Stream extraction and whole-field validation are different interfaces; do not claim that this operator rejects every trailing suffix by itself.

Extraction should parse into a candidate and commit only after the candidate is acceptable. In the quantity operator, failure to read an integer leaves the target unchanged. A representable integer outside the quantity domain sets failbit and also preserves the old value. The existing value remains available for the caller’s recovery logic.

This is token extraction, not whole-line validation. Reading an integer from 12ms can consume a numeric prefix and leave the suffix for a later operation. If the application requires the entire field to be a valid integer, use a parser that checks the full range, as the from_chars examples do. The same input can therefore be acceptable as the beginning of a stream token sequence and unacceptable as a complete numeric field. Name the grammar being tested.

Calling setstate can itself throw when the stream’s exception mask requests it. The operator’s preservation rule should still hold because it has not modified the target yet. Do not label extraction unconditionally noexcept just because the domain check looks simple. Stream policy participates in its behavior.
